newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH AFRICA - SEPT 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- South Africa's auditor general is investigating government payments totalling 1.2 billion rand to the oil industry, paid as compensation for market share lost to synthetic fuel production, amid claims that the industry overstated its opportunity costs.
- Finance officials were worried that the anticipated savings from downsizing the public sector would not materialise in the foreseeable future, sources said.

- The Small Business Development Corp's overall financing activities fell a quarter to 253 million rand in the year to March and could fall further this financial year following extensive restructuring.

- A Christian-backed satellite television network committed to entertainment free of sex, gratuitous violence or swearing will be launched in December following the Independent Broadcasting Authority's decision to approve the 350 million rand venture.

- An arms cache discovery on the West Rand in 1985 which led to a massive SADF raid on Gaborone had been a set-up devised by the SAP and the military, former Vlakplaas commander Eugene de Kock disclosed.

- Cement and building supplies group Alpha has significantly raised the stakes in its bid to rescue its planned merger with Blue Circle from a Competition Board veto by threatening to drop its plans to build an 800 million rand cement plant in Saldanha.
- The price war between airlines on routes between South Africa and London, caused by overcapacity during the winter months and new competition from Virgin Atlantic Airways, is all but over.
- The South African Futures Exchange has drawn up the specifications for a standard rand-dollar futures contract, which private traders would trade once exchange controls were sufficiently relaxed.

- Operations have ground to a complete halt on the key water transfer and hydro-electricity components of the $4.0 billion Lesotho Highlands Water Project after the sacking last week of half the project's workers and a bloody weekend clash with police.

- Nationalist cabinet ministers, top policemen, a homeland leader, a revered Communist Party boss, a top spy, a sitting senator and a host of lesser players were implicated in murder, cross-border raids, weapons smuggling and other clandestine operations by vonvicted killer Eugene de Kock, former chief of the police's notorious Vlakplaas counter-insurgency unit.

- A new satellite television network, free of "gratuitous violence, foul language and sex scenes" and based on fundamental Christian principles, has been temporarily licensed to broadcast seven digital channels bythe Indpendent Broadcasting Authority.
- Legislation to introduce abortion on request during the first 12 weeks of pregnancy was tabled in parliament yesterday. -- Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
